findings.where: absent from the set; and the whole of the rest of it — MANIFEST.json says browser: webkit, and every one of the seventeen scene logs says browser: webkit
findings.what: Nothing in the evidence shows a second platform: there is no Android screen anywhere, and the only cross-platform trace is two device-name strings in 05_settings.png ("android-capture", "pwa-mtuec711") which WHY_MISSING.json itself says is `dart run tool/host_daemon.dart` with no screen by construction, not a second copy of the app.
findings.why: The row's last clause — both platforms serve the same regions, the same feelings and the same event types — cannot be checked from the artifacts at all; the stated reason (no /dev/kvm, adbd answering after 113 minutes with no framework behind it) is a real reason for the missing screenshot, but it is not evidence for the claim, and the row asks for the claim.

findings.where: the lens row at y 300-390: WHAT WE SENT is underlined and set larger; WHAT HAPPENED and WHAT WE FELT stand unselected and are never photographed in any artifact
findings.what: Moments is shot in one of its three lenses. Its own report claims 154 events behind "what happened" and 1340 behind "what we felt", and not one of them is on the glass anywhere in the set; every tile in the artifact is a photo, a video or a voice note.
findings.why: The row asks whether the same event appears consistently across Chat, Moments and Us. A feeling is shown in Pulse, in Chat and landing on Us, and a to-do is shown in Us and in the Chat thread — but whether either reads the same in Moments is unphotographed, so a third of that comparison has no evidence behind it.

findings.where: coldstart.json `written_at` and reliability.json's `tailscale` block `checked_at`, both 2026-09-05T00:28; both carry `later_check: {"status": "pending", "why": "the nodes were not answering when this was re-run"}` dated 2026-09-09T17:42
findings.what: The only measurement of one log held identically on two devices across a tailnet — spine_host_order equal to spine_client_order, same_order_both_sides true, distinct node keys 100.68.254.25 and 100.72.198.108 — is four days older than this capture and could not be reproduced during it. Everything shot this run is one browser talking to a local host daemon over `transport: local`.
findings.why: "Exactly one event log and no second store anywhere" is a claim about two phones, and the two-phone half of it rests on a dated run whose re-check failed rather than on anything measured this cycle.

findings.where: THE SHELF block (card y1931-2144, strip y2156-2279) and the DATES block (card y292-496, strip y525-692)
findings.what: Three of the five module blocks print the same sentence twice within one block. The shelf card reads "waiting on you: the one you said you stopped" and the strip 12 px below it reads "the one you said you stopped"; the dates card prints "next: the place by the bridge" in full and the strip 29 px below truncates the same phrase mid-word to "the place by th…" to make room for "in 2 months"; the calendar card's "us in 60 days" and its strip's "us · 9 Nov" are the same fact twice.
findings.why: The repeated card-plus-strip unit is exactly what makes Us read as one system rather than five panels, and in three of its five instances the unit argues with itself — the glance restating the row, and the row cutting a word the card two centimetres above prints whole.

findings.where: the FEELINGS chip, the wedge at x 600-766, y 700-752
findings.what: An opaque near-black region sits over the desk at that chip's right end: 758 pixels below luma 30, minimum 4.3, where the desk immediately beside it measures 84-103. Every other chip on the screen shows desk through its torn edge; this one shows a hole.
findings.why: The chip row is the single artifact that best demonstrates the one log — eleven type chips including one per shared-life module — and one of the eleven is rendered broken, which is where a reader's confidence in the row goes.

findings.where: the standing ribbon, top 200 rows: it carries the status line, the place word, a NEED bar and an ENERGY bar and nothing else
findings.what: Two of the three state changes the clip drives never reach the everywhere-element. `state mood restless` shows only on the Pulse card (MOOD bright -> restless, frames 1 vs 165) and as a Chat thread row ("— noor is restless · Thu 3 Sep · 19:40", frame 305); `state availability heads_down`, driven at frame 10 of the last run, moves nothing visible. Only `state place out` moves the ribbon, TRAVELLING to OUT between frames 532 and 540.
findings.why: The row asks for partner state legible on every screen rather than only on Pulse. Place, need, energy and the standing line are legible everywhere; mood and availability are legible on Pulse and, for mood, in the thread — so on Moments and Settings the reader gets three of five signals.

what_is_working: One log with one cursor, and it is the same number everywhere: `events` reads 14062 in 01_pulse, 02_chat, 03_us, 04_moments, 05_settings, 12_search and crops/dusk_pulse alike, and afterwards grows only by what a scene writes — 14074 (13_messenger_states, twelve appends), 14075 (11_chat_scroll, 14_media_viewer), 14079 (06), 14081 (08), 14087 (07), 14092 (15). In all seventeen reports `sync.cursor` equals `events`, and Chat and Search report the same thread projection length (8069 of 8069, then 8075 after 13's appends), which is what a view onto one log looks like rather than two stores agreeing by luck.

Three independent records agree on a number only one store could produce: authored feelings = 2 in 01_pulse.report (`view.kinds.feeling_authored`), in 05_settings.report and 15_authored_feeling.report (`authored_feelings`), and in logs/haptics.check.json (`authored`); crops/haptics_strip.png then shows those two, `pigeon` and `tuesday soup`, sitting inside the same six families and on the same 2700 ms scale as the 34 built-ins rather than in a compartment of their own.

An arithmetic identity across three separate reports: Moments' `milestones` lens counts 154, which is exactly dates 81 + calendar 6 + rituals 53 + shelf 12 (03_us.report) + authored feelings 2 (01_pulse.report). The lens is not a second table; it is a filter over the same events Us is reading.

Every module is in three registries at once and in the same shape in all three: five index cards in 03_us, each 708 or 709 px wide at x 365-366 with a stamped name, a one-line glance and one torn thread strip below it; five module chips (TO DO, DATES, DATES THAT MATTER, RITUALS, THE SHELF) among the fifteen in 12_search; and a notification row per event kind in 05_settings, matching logs/reception.json's `by_type` map of eighteen kinds whose values agree with the screen (reaction quiet, feeling wake-me, state_declared quiet). logs/reliability.json then answers nine search queries, one per type, three of them module types (todo_event 'bread', date_event 'ferry', milestone 'together').

Chat is visibly a view onto everything rather than a message list. In one throw of 11_chat_scroll.mp4 the thread carries a photo ("long day"), a feeling drawn as the same pink sweet Pulse uses for `nyeh`, a to-do on ruled paper with a real checkbox ("the pressure at hers again, and find out"), a passive state line ("noor's phone is on normal") and written notes; its report names feeling, message and todo_event at the anchor. 08_state_propagating.mp4 renders the partner's declared mood as a thread row in the margin hand — "— noor is restless · Thu 3 Sep · 19:40" — while messages sit on paper, a distinction it keeps in 11 as well.

The shell is one component, measured: the top 200 rows of 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 12 and 13 are pixel-identical (mean absolute difference 0.00 against 01_pulse); 10_first_run and 17_setup_pwa carry the unpaired variant of the same ribbon ("nothing from them yet. the six words are on the other phone."); 14_media_viewer, a modal, is the only artifact without it. In the bottom 170 rows, exactly two 269-px tab cells differ between Pulse and Chat (x 28-296 and x 306-574) and nothing else moves.

One event type renders as one component in two regions: the voice note in 02_chat draws 48 waveform bars at 10.0 px pitch and in 04_moments 50 bars at 4.5 px — the same play triangle, the same right-aligned duration, the same metadata line beneath, scaled to its container rather than drawn twice. Search results are written in the author's own hand exactly as the thread is: Noor's slanted (median stroke-gradient 12.5 deg in 12_search, 6.0 deg in 02_chat) against Teo's upright (0.0 and 2.4 deg).

A feeling is one event in three views. 07_feeling_landing.mp4 shows it arrive as a large object over the Pulse card, take its place in the Pulse object strip, appear in Chat as a thread row ("a squeeze · Thu 3 Sep · 20:01"), and land again over the Us module list; 15_authored_feeling.mp4 opens the same picker over Us and the resulting object lands on Pulse and on Settings. The six objects on 01_pulse carry the same clock times as `recent_feelings` in its report to the minute (21:58, 06:42, 11:54, 16:23, 16:58, 17:19), and name the author only when the author is not the reader — teo's two carry no name, noor's four carry hers.

The whole language holds under a second light: crops/dusk_pulse.png is the same ribbon, card, object strip, own-state sheet and tab bar with the desk and paper warmed, and its report carries the same `events: 14062`.
verdict: Read only from the pictures and the records, this is one system and not an assembly, and the evidence for that is arithmetic rather than impression: one `events` count (14062) in every region report and one `sync.cursor` equal to it; one thread projection whose length Chat and Search both report as 8069; Moments' 'what happened' lens equal to the sum of four modules' events plus the two authored feelings; three separate records agreeing that exactly two feelings were authored. Every module appears in three registries in the same shape — a 708-px index card in Us, a chip in Search, a notification row in Settings — so a sixth would slot into three lists that already treat five identically, and the thread proves the modules write into the same log rather than beside it, because a to-do turns up in Chat on ruled paper with a checkbox and a declared mood turns up as a margin row. The shell is one component to the pixel (the top 200 rows identical across seven artifacts; two tab cells and nothing else moving between regions), and one event type draws as one component at two sizes across Chat and Moments. What holds the row at its floor rather than above it is what cannot be seen: no Android screen exists anywhere in the set, so half the row's last clause has no artifact behind it and rests on two device-name strings; Moments is photographed in one of its three lenses, so a third of the cross-region comparison the row asks for is missing; and the only two-device measurement of the one log is four days old with a failed re-check. Two smaller things cost it as well — three of the five Us module blocks say the same sentence twice, one of them truncating mid-word a phrase the card above prints whole, and the FEELINGS chip in Search renders with an opaque hole. Nothing here is blocking: the row meets its floor at 13, and no finding contradicts the one-log claim; they only leave parts of it unwitnessed. One thing I checked that is not a fault of the app: frames.json marks 08_state_propagating `ok: false` for one brightness jump, and it is frame 305, mean luma 123.7 between 153.5 and 155.5, the first frame after the run cut at 304 — a seam in how the picture was taken, not a flash in the app.
